text:
A: Hiya! I'm Gemma. How's your day going?
B: Hi. Riya. It's fine, thanks. Busy week.
A: Oh, I know that feeling. Where are you based?
B: Canada Water, South-East London. You?
A: Warrington. North West. Sorry, I've been saying that all afternoon, I sound like a recording.
B: That's the format, I suppose. What do you do?
A: Office and accounts admin for a scaffolding firm. Purchase ledger, timesheets, hire paperwork, all that. Not very exciting, I'll be honest.
B: It's more important than people think. Whoever controls the paperwork usually knows more about the business than the directors.
A: Ha, I'd never say that out loud, but yeah, sort of. What about you?
B: Operations manager for a grocery delivery company. Fulfilment planning for two warehouses. Mostly capacity models and forecasting.
A: Oh, so spreadsheets, then? I love a spreadsheet. I taught myself pivot tables off YouTube, which the boss thinks is magic.
B: Self-taught is how most people learn them, honestly. Do you use Power Query at all, or just tables?
A: Erm, I don't really know what that is, to be honest.
B: It pulls data in and cleans it automatically. If you're reconciling timesheets by hand every week, it would probably save you a few hours.
A: Oh, would it? I do them a day early so I'm never caught out, but that'd be lovely. Is it hard?
B: Not for someone who taught themselves pivot tables. Give it an afternoon.
A: I might, actually. Are you very organised outside work as well, or is that just me?
B: That depends what you mean by organised. I plan my week on Sunday, batch cook, book Pilates three weeks out. So, probably yes.
A: Oh, I batch cook on a Sunday! Chilli, lasagne for the freezer, scouse when it's cold. What do you make?
B: Dal, poha, which is flattened rice, Maharashtrian. And grain bowls. Enough for five lunches.
A: Five lunches, that's very disciplined. Craig, my husband, would eat all five on Monday night. Do you do your holidays on a spreadsheet as well?
B: Always. I'm planning Seoul for next spring. There's a tab for each day.
A: Stop! Tenerife's on a spreadsheet already, and we're not going till next year. Everyone at netball laughs at me.
B: They'll be the ones asking you where the hotel is.
A: Ha, they are, every time. So is it a big team you've got?
B: Seven. Planners and shift leads. I'm hoping for Head of Operations in the next couple of years, ideally somewhere bigger.
A: Oh, good for you. I'd quite like office manager eventually, but I'm not, you know, pushing for it. I'd just like to feel secure.
B: Have you told them you want it?
A: Erm, not as such. The owner's daughter is sort of in that role, so
